senses.gloss: f. (פוק) = b. h. פּוּקָה, gliding, sinking.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 147b:14">Sabb. 147ᵇ</cite> <he>משום פ׳</he> on account of sinking in the clay-soil (<cite ref="Q00678"><he>פִּילוֹמָא</he></cite>, which makes walking a labor; Rashi: he might stain his garments when sinking in the muddy soil, and then wring them out).—

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 7:21">Tosef. ib. VII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 8:21">VIII</cite>), 21 <he>מבעיתין לעוית ולפ׳ וכ׳</he> (Var. <he>ולפוקה</he>) you may shock a person in convulsions, or in an attack of vertigo, and it is not forbidden as a superstitious practice, v. <cite ref="A02007"><he>אֱמוֹרִי</he></cite>.—

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 1054:12">Yalk. Esth. 1054</cite> <he>מכניסין פ׳ בממונו וכ׳</he> they (the Jews) cause a sinking (decline) in the wealth of the world (<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 7:12">Esth. R. to III, 8</cite> <cite ref="Q00488"><he>פַּחַת</he></cite>).—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 111b:5">Snh. 111ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>פקו</he>, <cite ref="Isaiah 28:7">Is. XXVIII, 7</cite>) <he>אין פוקה אלא גהינם</he> (Ms. K. <he>פקו</he>) ‘sinking’ means going to Gehenna.
